result.topic_en: Derivation of the integrability conditions (Riemann curvature quantities (ii',i''i''')) that the coefficients b of a quadratic differential form must satisfy if it can be transformed into a sum of squares, and their expression via second variations.
result.transcription:
14.
$\sum_\nu \frac{\partial s_\iota}{\partial x_\nu}\frac{\partial x_\nu}{\partial s_{\iota'}} = 0$, si $\iota \gtrless \iota'$
(3) $\sum \frac{\partial x}{\partial s_\iota}\frac{\partial x}{\partial s_{\iota'}} = b_{\iota,\iota'}$ (4) $\sum \frac{\partial s_\iota}{\partial x}\frac{\partial s_{\iota'}}{\partial x} = \frac{\beta_{\iota,\iota'}}{B}$
et differentiando formulam (3)
$\sum \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota''}}\frac{\partial x}{\partial s_{\iota'}} + \sum \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}}\frac{\partial x}{\partial s_\iota} = \frac{\partial b_{\iota,\iota'}}{\partial s_{\iota''}}$
Jam ex his ipsarum $\frac{\partial b_{\iota,\iota'}}{\partial s_{\iota''}}$, $\frac{\partial b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}}$, $\frac{\partial b_{\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_\iota}$
expressionibus eruitur
(5) $2\sum \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}}\frac{\partial x}{\partial s_\iota} = \frac{\partial b_{\iota,\iota'}}{\partial s_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}} - \frac{\partial b_{\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_\iota}$
et si haec quantitas per $p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}$ designatur
(6) $2\frac{\partial^2 x_\nu}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial s_\iota}{\partial x_\nu} p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}$
Quantitatibus $p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}$ iterum differentiatis obtinetur
$\frac{\partial p_{\iota,\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'''}} - \frac{\partial p_{\iota,\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota''}} = 2\sum \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}}\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota'''}} - 2\sum \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota'''}}\frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota''}}$
unde tandem prodit, substitutis valoribus modo inventis (6) et (4)
(I.) $\frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota'''}} +$
$\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\nu,\nu'}(p_{\nu,\iota,\iota'''}\, p_{\nu',\iota',\iota''} - p_{\nu,\iota,\iota''}\, p_{\nu',\iota',\iota'''})\frac{\beta_{\nu,\nu'}}{B} = 0$
Hujusmodi igitur aequationibus functiones $b$ satisfaciant necesse est, quando $\sum_{\iota\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$ in formam $\sum_\iota dx_\iota^2$ transformari potest: partes laevas harum aequationum designabimus per
$(\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')$.
Ut indoles harum aequationum melius perspiciatur, formetur expressio
$\delta\delta \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'} - 2\, d\delta \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'} + dd \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'}$
determinatis variationibus secundi [-gradus-] ordinis $d^2$, $d\delta$, $\delta^2$ ita, ut sit:
$\delta' \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'} - \delta \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, \delta' s_{\iota'} - d \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota\, \delta' s_{\iota'} = 0$
$\delta' \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'} - 2\, d \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, \delta' s_{\iota'} = 0$
$\delta' \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'} - 2\, \delta \sum b_{\iota,\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota\, \delta' s_{\iota'} = 0$
denotante $\delta'$ variationem quamcunque. Quo pacto haec expressio invenietur
(II) $= \sum (\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')(ds_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'} - ds_{\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota)(ds_{\iota''}\, \delta s_{\iota'''} - ds_{\iota'''}\, \delta s_{\iota''})$

methods.quote: (I.) $\frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota'''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota,\iota'''}}{\partial s_{\iota'}\partial s_{\iota''}} - \frac{\partial^2 b_{\iota',\iota''}}{\partial s_\iota \partial s_{\iota'''}} +$

items.quote: Hujusmodi igitur aequationibus functiones $b$ satisfaciant necesse est, quando $\sum_{\iota\iota'} b_{\iota,\iota'}\, ds_\iota\, ds_{\iota'}$ in formam $\sum_\iota dx_\iota^2$ transformari potest
items.english: The functions b must therefore satisfy equations of this kind whenever the form sum b ds ds can be transformed into the form sum dx^2.

items.quote:
Quo pacto haec expressio invenietur
(II) $= \sum (\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')(ds_\iota\, \delta s_{\iota'} - ds_{\iota'}\, \delta s_\iota)(ds_{\iota''}\, \delta s_{\iota'''} - ds_{\iota'''}\, \delta s_{\iota''})$
items.english: In this way this expression will be found to equal the sum of (ii',i''i''') times the products of the bivectors.
